title: Enterprise Onboarding, Escalation & QBR Playbook (v2)
author: Maya Patel
body:
Summary:
This playbook standardizes how Customer Success (CS), Support, and Engineering collaborate during enterprise onboarding, manage escalations, and run health checks and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs). It consolidates the phased onboarding checklist, escalation matrices and SLAs, integration guidance for common connectivity patterns, a curated set of known issues and workarounds, and QBR/health-check templates.

Purpose and scope:
- Audience: CS Managers, Solutions Engineers, Support L2/L3, Customer Success Engineers (CSEs), and customer technical leads.
- Scope: Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding to Redwood Inference (Dedicated or Private deployments) and hosted customers with enterprise SLAs.

Quick links:
- Integration templates: confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026
- Escalation procedures: confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-escalation-playbook-2025
- Known issues index: confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-known-issues-workarounds-support-process-2026

1) Onboarding phases (overview)
Each enterprise onboarding follows five phases. Owner indicated in parentheses.
1. Pre-contract / Discovery (CS Lead)
   - Capture technical constraints: VPC, egress requirements, data residency, regulatory controls, KMS/HSM needs.
   - Deliverable: Technical Requirements Checklist (see table).
2. Kickoff & Design (CSE / Solutions Eng)
   - Align on architecture, network diagrams, rollout plan, and success metrics.
   - Schedule 90-day plan and identify primary contacts and on-call windows.
3. Integration & Validation (Customer + CSE)
   - Implement network peering / VPN, API keys, routing rules, and test prompts/workloads.
   - Run smoke tests and runbook walkthroughs; document failures.
4. Ramp & Performance Tuning (CS + Eng Platform)
   - Configure batching, quantization profiles, autoscale policies. Monitor cost/latency tradeoffs.
   - Gate: 7-day stability with SLO adherence before move to prod.
5. Production & QBR Cadence (CS Lead)
   - Hand-off to success plan, schedule monthly health checks and quarterly QBRs.

Technical Requirements Checklist (table):
| Item | Required / Optional | Notes | Owner |
|-----|-----:|-----|-----|
| Network connectivity (VPC peering / IPSec) | Required | CIDR ranges, egress rules, proxy | Customer / CSE |
| API credentials & RBAC | Required | Create service account with least privilege | Customer |
| Data residency / retention | Required (if regulated) | Specify region(s), retention TTLs | Customer / Security |
| KMS/HSM integration | Optional | For Private deployments, provide KMS endpoints | Customer / Security |
| Test corpus and prompts | Required | Representative prompt sets for eval | Customer / CSE |
| Traffic profile (RPS, seq len) | Required | 95th pct concurrent requests and latency targets | Customer |

2) Integration guidance (common patterns)
- Hosted API integration (fastest path)
  - Create API key in Console -> Integrations -> API Keys.
  - Sample curl:
    curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-3b","input":"Hello"}'
- Dedicated / Private deployment patterns
  - Network: Allow egress to Redwood control plane IPs for licensing; inference traffic remains on private network.
  - Credentials: Use short-lived certs or mutual TLS where configured.
- Common pitfalls and mitigations
  - DNS / proxy timeouts: Default proxy idle timeout of 60s can drop streaming responses — recommend keepalives and proxy config change to 5m for streaming routes.
  - Large context windows: Ensure LB and routing allow >60s requests for long-generation flows.

3) Escalation matrix and runbook
Severity definitions and target response times (enterprise SLAs):
- Sev 1 (Critical): Production outage impacting >30% of requests or complete loss of inference. Response: 15 minutes, Target restore: 2 hours.
- Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation in latency or errors affecting a segment. Response: 1 hour, Target restore: 8 hours.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Functional bug, degraded quality, or intermittent errors. Response: 8 business hours, Target restore: 3 business days.
- Sev 4 (Low): General questions, feature requests. Response: 2 business days.

Escalation steps (concrete):
1. Triage in Support (L1): gather logs, customer request ID, timestamp, model & route, sample payload, and recent console traces.
2. If suspected infra/runtime bug, escalate to Eng Platform or Serving Runtime (L2) with incident runbook link.
3. For confirmed customer-impacting Sev1/Sev2, notify PagerDuty, schedule a bridge, and inform CS Lead and Sales. Use incident-bridge@redwood.ai template.
4. Post-incident: create postmortem (owner: Eng SRE) within 3 business days for Sev1, 7 days for Sev2. Share summary with customer and include mitigation plan and timeline.

Contacts and ownership (example):
- CS Lead: Primary customer-facing owner.
- CSE: Integration and technical coordination.
- Support L2: Initial escalation target for runtime errors.
- Eng SRE / Runtime: Pager on-call for Sev1.
- Escalation email: enterprise-escalations@redwood.ai

4) Known issues & workarounds (selected entries)
- Issue: Occasional tokenization mismatch on older model variants.
  - Symptom: Off-by-one token counts in embeddings causing alignment errors.
  - Workaround: Force model variant with updated tokenizer (append query parameter model_variant=tokenfix) and re-run ingestion.
- Issue: Intermittent 502s from proxy under sustained streaming load.
  - Symptom: Streaming connections dropped after 60s.
  - Workaround: Increase proxy idle timeout to 300s and enable chunked transfer encoding.
- Issue: High tail latency for large-batch synchronous calls.
  - Symptom: 99th pct latency spikes during batch peaks.
  - Workaround: Move to async batch endpoints and increase concurrency targets; configure autoscale policy to add warm GPUs at 70% utilization.

(Full Known Issues index is maintained at confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-known-issues-workarounds-support-process-2026)

5) Support process & triage checklist
When a customer files a ticket, Support L1 must:
- Confirm customer identity and subscription tier.
- Record: request_id, timestamps, model, route, input sample, expected/actual output, SDK/runtime version, region, and logs (if provided).
- Reproduce: attempt to reproduce in staging with representative prompt; capture traces.
- Escalate: follow severity matrix if reproduction shows production impact.

Triage template (copy into ticket):
- Customer:
- Contact:
- Environment: (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
- Model & version:
- Route name:
- Request ID / Timestamp:
- Steps to reproduce:
- Attachments: logs, sample prompt, screenshots

6) Health checks and QBR materials
Monthly health-check agenda (30–60m):
- Roll call & agenda (5m)
- Operational metrics (15m): request rate, error rate, 95/99 latency, token cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, autoscale events.
- Recent incidents & mitigations (5–10m)
- Product/roadmap items (5–10m)
- Actions & owners (5m)

Quarterly Business Review (QBR) template:
1. Executive summary: adoption, value delivered, business KPIs.
2. Operational review: availability, latency SLOs, utilization, cost trends.
3. Model quality: evals on representative prompt sets, regression alerts, recent tuning.
4. Roadmap & feature asks: planned platform changes, dedicated deployment timeline.
5. Risk & compliance: outstanding security items, audit readiness.
6. Action items and next steps (owner + target date).

Suggested QBR metrics (pull from Console dashboards):
- Availability (monthly uptime % and SLO drift)
- 95th / 99th latency by route and model
- Error rate (5xx / 4xx) and root causes
- Tokens served / cost per 1k tokens
- Cache hit ratio and inferred cost savings
- Model drift / eval regression count

7) Post-onboarding handoff checklist
- Confirm monitoring & alerting ownership transferred to customer or CS (depending on SLA).
- Provide runbook links and credentials for support tools.
- Schedule first QBR and recurring monthly health checks.
- Document agreed SLAs and escalation contacts in the customer record.

Appendices
A. Runbook links & templates:
- Sev1 runbook: confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/sev1-incident-response
- Postmortem template: confluence/eng-sre/incident-review/postmortem-template
- Integration checklist (detailed): confluence/customer-success-and-support/enterprise-onboarding-integration-playbook-2026

B. Onboarding checklist (copyable)
- [ ] Technical discovery completed
- [ ] Network & security approvals obtained
- [ ] API keys issued and validated
- [ ] Smoke tests passed (latency & correctness)
- [ ] Autoscale policy configured and tested
- [ ] QBR cadence scheduled

C. Contact matrix (copyable)
- CS Lead: cs-lead@redwood.ai
- CSE / Solutions Eng: solutions-eng@redwood.ai
- Support: support@redwood.ai
- Enterprise escalations: enterprise-escalations@redwood.ai

Notes and maintenance
- Owner: Customer Success Documentation Guild (Customer Success)
- Review cadence: annually, or after any Sev1 postmortem.
- Change log: maintain a short changelog in the page comments for small edits; major revisions must include reviewers and be dated.

End of document.
